conn = sqlite3.connect(r"C:\CHURN_ANALYSIS\customer_churn.db")

sql_query="""
    SELECT name
    FROM sqlite_master
    WHERE type='table'

    """
tables= pd.read_sql(sql_query,conn)

# create dataframe for each table
for table_name in tables['name']:
    df = pd.read_sql(f"SELECT * from {table_name}",conn)
    globals() [f"df_{table_name}"]=df
    print(f" Created dataframe: df_{table_name}")

# Print table names and Column names
conn = sqlite3.connect(r"C:\CHURN_ANALYSIS\customer_churn.db")

for table_name in tables['name']:
    print(f"\nTable Name: {table_name}")
    # Get Column information
    columns_query = f"PRAGMA table_info({table_name});"
    columns=pd.read_sql(columns_query,conn)
    print("Columns:")
    print(columns['name'].tolist())

# close connection
conn.close()

)

#12. create a column using existing column - churn risk

    (df['churn_score'] < 50),
    (df['churn_score'] >= 50) & (df['churn_score'] < 70),
    (df['churn_score'] >= 70)
]

df['churn_risk'] = np.select(conditions,risk_level,default='unknown')

# A. MONTHLY CHURN TREND(Time series kpi)

df_visual['cancellation_month'] = df_visual['cancellation_date'].dt.to_period('M')

churn_trend = (
    df_visual[df_visual['churn_flag'] == 1]
    .groupby('cancellation_month')
    .size()
)

plt.figure(figsize=(14,6))

plt.plot(
    churn_trend.index.astype(str),
    churn_trend.values,
    color='green',
    marker='o',
    linestyle='dashed',
    linewidth=2,
    markersize=6
)

plt.title("Monthly Churn Trend",fontsize=15, fontweight="bold")
plt.xlabel("Month", fontsize=12)

In [66]:
# CORRECT method of encoding - BASED ON PRIORITY

df_encoded = df_visual[['plan_type', 'contract_type', 'churn_score', 'churn_flag', 'churn_risk', 'escalations']]

order_mappings = {
    'plan_type' : ['Basic', 'Standard', 'Premium'],
    'contract_type' : ['Monthly', 'Annual'],
    'churn_risk' : ['low', 'med', 'high']
}

for col, order in order_mappings.items():
    df_encoded[col] = pd.Categorical(df_encoded[col].astype('category'),categories=order,ordered=True).codes

<h1 id="%F0%9F%93%8A-Revenue-Analytics-%E2%80%93-Executive-Summary">📊 Revenue Analytics – Executive Summary¶</h1><hr /> <h2 id="%F0%9F%8E%AF-Business-Objective">🎯 Business Objective¶</h2><p>Evaluate how revenue is distributed across customer segments, subscription plans, contract types, and geographic regions to identify high-value customers, major revenue contributors, and potential revenue leakage due to customer churn.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="%F0%9F%94%8D-Key-Insights">🔍 Key Insights¶</h2><h3 id="%F0%9F%92%B0-Revenue-Contribution-by-Plan">💰 Revenue Contribution by Plan¶</h3>
  • Premium plans generated the highest share of total monthly revenue despite serving a comparatively smaller customer base.
  • Higher average monthly charges and CLTV indicate that premium subscribers contribute significantly more revenue per customer.
<hr /> <h3 id="%F0%9F%8C%8D-Geographic-Revenue-Distribution">🌍 Geographic Revenue Distribution¶</h3>
  • Revenue is concentrated in a limited number of states, with the top-performing regions contributing a substantial share of overall revenue.
  • These regions represent strategic markets for customer retention and targeted marketing initiatives.
<hr /> <h3 id="%F0%9F%93%89-Revenue-Loss-Due-to-Churn">📉 Revenue Loss Due to Churn¶</h3>
  • Customers on Monthly contracts accounted for a disproportionately high share of revenue lost through churn.
  • This suggests that shorter contract commitments are associated with higher customer attrition and increased revenue leakage.
<hr /> <h3 id="%F0%9F%91%91-High-Value-Customers">👑 High-Value Customers¶</h3>
  • The top 10 customers exhibited significantly higher Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) compared to the overall customer base.
  • Protecting these high-value customers through personalized engagement and loyalty initiatives can maximize long-term profitability.
<hr /> <h3 id="%F0%9F%93%88-Revenue-Concentration-(Pareto-Analysis)">📈 Revenue Concentration (Pareto Analysis)¶</h3>
  • Revenue follows the Pareto Principle, where a relatively small percentage of states contribute the majority of total revenue.
  • Prioritizing customer acquisition and retention efforts in these high-performing regions can deliver the greatest business impact.
<hr /> <h2 id="%F0%9F%92%BC-Business-Recommendations">💼 Business Recommendations¶</h2>
  • Increase adoption of Premium subscription plans through personalized upgrade campaigns.
  • Strengthen retention programs for Monthly contract customers to reduce revenue leakage.
  • Launch region-specific marketing campaigns targeting high-revenue states.
  • Develop VIP retention strategies for customers with the highest CLTV.
  • Allocate marketing and customer success resources based on revenue contribution rather than customer volume alone.
<hr /> <h2 id="%F0%9F%93%8C-Conclusion">📌 Conclusion¶</h2><p>The revenue analysis reveals that customer value is unevenly distributed across plans, contracts, and geographic regions. Focusing retention efforts on high-value customers and high-revenue markets, while reducing churn among Monthly contract users, presents the greatest opportunity to improve long-term revenue and customer lifetime value.</p>

# CUSTOMER SEGMENTATION

def customer_segment(row):

    # Champions
    if row["cltv"] >= df["cltv"].quantile(0.75) and row["churn_risk"] == "Low":
        return "Champion"

    # High Value
    elif row["cltv"] >= df["cltv"].quantile(0.75):
        return "High Value"

    # Loyal
    elif row["tenure_days"] >= df["tenure_days"].quantile(0.75):
        return "Loyal"

    # At Risk
    elif row["churn_risk"] == "High":
        return "At Risk"

    # New Customers
    elif row["tenure_days"] <= df["tenure_days"].quantile(0.25):
        return "New Customer"

    else:
        return "Regular"


df["customer_segment"] = df.apply(customer_segment, axis=1)

display(df[["customerid","customer_segment"]].head())

<h1 id="%F0%9F%8E%AF-Customer-Segmentation-%E2%80%93-Executive-Summary">🎯 Customer Segmentation – Executive Summary¶</h1><hr /> <h2 id="Business-Objective">Business Objective¶</h2><p>Identify distinct customer groups based on customer lifetime value (CLTV), tenure, and churn risk to support targeted retention, engagement, and revenue optimization strategies.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="Key-Insights">Key Insights¶</h2>
  • Champions represent the company's most valuable customers with high CLTV and low churn risk.
  • High Value customers generate substantial revenue but require proactive engagement to reduce churn.
  • Loyal customers demonstrate long-term commitment and provide stable recurring revenue.
  • At Risk customers show elevated churn probability and should be prioritized for retention campaigns.
  • New Customers require effective onboarding to improve long-term retention.
<hr /> <h2 id="Business-Recommendations">Business Recommendations¶</h2>
  • Offer exclusive rewards and premium services to Champion customers.
  • Design personalized retention campaigns for At Risk customers.
  • Encourage High Value customers to adopt longer-term contracts.
  • Improve onboarding and early engagement for New Customers.
  • Allocate marketing budgets based on customer segment profitability and churn risk.
<hr /> <h2 id="Conclusion">Conclusion¶</h2><p>Customer segmentation enables the business to move from one-size-fits-all marketing to data-driven customer relationship management, maximizing customer lifetime value while reducing churn.</p>

<h1 id="%F0%9F%94%8D-Churn-Driver-Analysis-%E2%80%93-Executive-Summary">🔍 Churn Driver Analysis – Executive Summary¶</h1><h2 id="Objective">Objective¶</h2><p>Identify the key factors associated with customer churn to support targeted retention strategies.</p> <h2 id="Key-Insights">Key Insights¶</h2>
  • Churn varies significantly across subscription plans, indicating that pricing and feature offerings influence customer retention.
  • Customers on shorter-duration contracts exhibit higher churn rates than those on long-term contracts.
  • Higher complaint counts and escalated support cases are strongly associated with increased churn.
  • Lower CSAT scores correspond to higher churn, highlighting the importance of customer satisfaction.
  • Certain states consistently report higher churn rates, suggesting regional differences in customer behavior.
<h2 id="Business-Recommendations">Business Recommendations¶</h2>
  • Prioritize retention campaigns for high-risk plans and monthly contract customers.
  • Reduce complaint resolution time and proactively manage escalated cases.
  • Improve customer support quality to increase CSAT scores.
  • Investigate operational or market-specific issues in high-churn states.
  • Develop targeted interventions for customer segments exhibiting multiple churn risk factors.
<h2 id="Conclusion">Conclusion¶</h2><p>Churn is influenced by a combination of customer behavior, contract characteristics, service quality, and geographic factors. Addressing these drivers can significantly improve retention and protect recurring revenue.</p>

def cohort_index(row):

    return (
        (row["ActivityMonth"].year - row["CohortMonth"].year)*12
        +
        (row["ActivityMonth"].month - row["CohortMonth"].month)
    )

df["CohortIndex"] = df.apply(
    cohort_index,
    axis=1
)

<h1 id="%F0%9F%93%85-Cohort-Analysis-%E2%80%93-Executive-Summary">📅 Cohort Analysis – Executive Summary¶</h1><h2 id="Business-Objective">Business Objective¶</h2><p>Evaluate customer retention patterns over time by grouping customers based on their subscription start month (cohort). This helps identify whether newer customer cohorts are retained better or worse than earlier cohorts.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="Key-Insights">Key Insights¶</h2>
  • Customer retention declines gradually as cohorts age, which is expected in subscription-based businesses.
  • Some cohorts demonstrate stronger long-term retention, suggesting that acquisition timing, marketing campaigns, or customer onboarding strategies may have influenced customer loyalty.
  • The retention heatmap clearly highlights periods where customer drop-off is most significant.
  • Average retention trends provide an overview of how quickly customers disengage over time.
<hr /> <h2 id="Business-Recommendations">Business Recommendations¶</h2>
  • Strengthen onboarding programs during the first few months after customer acquisition.
  • Identify best-performing cohorts and replicate the acquisition or engagement strategies used for those customers.
  • Introduce targeted retention campaigns before the months where the highest customer drop-off occurs.
  • Continuously monitor cohort performance to evaluate the effectiveness of future retention initiatives.
<hr /> <h2 id="Conclusion">Conclusion¶</h2><p>Cohort analysis provides a time-based view of customer retention that is more informative than overall churn metrics. It enables the business to understand customer lifecycle behavior and supports data-driven retention strategies.</p>

from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

churned = df[df["churn_flag"] == 1]["monthly_charges"]
retained = df[df["churn_flag"] == 0]["monthly_charges"]

    churned,
    retained,
    equal_var=False
)

print(f"P-value: {p:.4f}")

  • Subscription plan was tested to identify if certain plans experience significantly different churn behavior.
  • Monthly charges were compared between churned and retained customers to assess whether pricing influences churn.
<h3 id="Business-Value">Business Value¶</h3><p>The results help prioritize retention strategies based on statistically validated evidence rather than descriptive observations alone.</p>

    treatment_churn,
    size=int(len(treatment_churn) * 0.20),
    replace=False
)

<h1 id="%F0%9F%A7%AA-A/B-Testing-Simulation-%E2%80%93-Executive-Summary">🧪 A/B Testing Simulation – Executive Summary¶</h1><h2 id="Business-Objective">Business Objective¶</h2><p>Evaluate whether offering a 10% retention discount to high-risk customers can reduce customer churn.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="Experiment-Design">Experiment Design¶</h2>
  • Selected customers with High Churn Risk.
  • Randomly assigned them into:
    • Control Group: No discount.
    • Treatment Group: Simulated 10% retention discount.
  • Compared churn rates between the two groups.
  • Used a Chi-Square Test to determine whether the difference was statistically significant.
<hr /> <h2 id="Key-Findings">Key Findings¶</h2>
  • The Treatment Group showed a lower churn rate than the Control Group.
  • The statistical test was used to evaluate whether the observed difference was significant.
<hr /> <h2 id="Business-Recommendation">Business Recommendation¶</h2><p>If a real-world A/B test produces similar results, the company should consider offering targeted retention discounts to high-risk customers while monitoring long-term profitability.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="Note">Note¶</h2><p>This is a simulated A/B test created for educational purposes to demonstrate experimental design and statistical evaluation.</p>

penalty penalty: {'l1', 'l2', 'elasticnet', None}, default='l2'<br><br>Specify the norm of the penalty:<br><br>- `None`: no penalty is added;<br>- `'l2'`: add a L2 penalty term and it is the default choice;<br>- `'l1'`: add a L1 penalty term;<br>- `'elasticnet'`: both L1 and L2 penalty terms are added.<br><br>.. warning::<br> Some penalties may not work with some solvers. See the parameter<br> `solver` below, to know the compatibility between the penalty and<br> solver.<br><br>.. versionadded:: 0.19<br> l1 penalty with SAGA solver (allowing 'multinomial' + L1)<br><br>.. deprecated:: 1.8<br> `penalty` was deprecated in version 1.8 and will be removed in 1.10.<br> Use `l1_ratio` instead. `l1_ratio=0` for `penalty='l2'`, `l1_ratio=1` for<br> `penalty='l1'` and `l1_ratio` set to any float between 0 and 1 for<br> `'penalty='elasticnet'`. 'deprecated'
C C: float, default=1.0<br><br>Inverse of regularization strength; must be a positive float.<br>Like in support vector machines, smaller values specify stronger<br>regularization. `C=np.inf` results in unpenalized logistic regression.<br>For a visual example on the effect of tuning the `C` parameter<br>with an L1 penalty, see:<br>:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_logistic_path.py`. 1.0
l1_ratio l1_ratio: float, default=0.0<br><br>The Elastic-Net mixing parameter, with `0 <= l1_ratio <= 1`. Setting<br>`l1_ratio=1` gives a pure L1-penalty, setting `l1_ratio=0` a pure L2-penalty.<br>Any value between 0 and 1 gives an Elastic-Net penalty of the form<br>`l1_ratio * L1 + (1 - l1_ratio) * L2`.<br><br>.. warning::<br> Certain values of `l1_ratio`, i.e. some penalties, may not work with some<br> solvers. See the parameter `solver` below, to know the compatibility between<br> the penalty and solver.<br><br>.. versionchanged:: 1.8<br> Default value changed from None to 0.0.<br><br>.. deprecated:: 1.8<br> `None` is deprecated and will be removed in version 1.10. Always use<br> `l1_ratio` to specify the penalty type. 0.0
dual dual: bool, default=False<br><br>Dual (constrained) or primal (regularized, see also<br>:ref:`this equation <regularized-logistic-loss>`) formulation. Dual formulation<br>is only implemented for l2 penalty with liblinear solver. Prefer `dual=False`<br>when n_samples > n_features. False
tol tol: float, default=1e-4<br><br>Tolerance for stopping criteria. 0.0001
fit_intercept fit_intercept: bool, default=True<br><br>Specifies if a constant (a.k.a. bias or intercept) should be<br>added to the decision function. True
intercept_scaling intercept_scaling: float, default=1<br><br>Useful only when the solver `liblinear` is used<br>and `self.fit_intercept` is set to `True`. In this case, `x` becomes<br>`[x, self.intercept_scaling]`,<br>i.e. a "synthetic" feature with constant value equal to<br>`intercept_scaling` is appended to the instance vector.<br>The intercept becomes<br>``intercept_scaling * synthetic_feature_weight``.<br><br>.. note::<br> The synthetic feature weight is subject to L1 or L2<br> regularization as all other features.<br> To lessen the effect of regularization on synthetic feature weight<br> (and therefore on the intercept) `intercept_scaling` has to be increased. 1
class_weight class_weight: dict or 'balanced', default=None<br><br>Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.<br>If not given, all classes are supposed to have weight one.<br><br>The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust<br>weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data<br>as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``.<br><br>Note that these weights will be multiplied with sample_weight (passed<br>through the fit method) if sample_weight is specified.<br><br>.. versionadded:: 0.17<br> *class_weight='balanced'* None
random_state random_state: int, RandomState instance, default=None<br><br>Used when ``solver`` == 'sag', 'saga' or 'liblinear' to shuffle the<br>data. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details. None
solver solver: {'lbfgs', 'liblinear', 'newton-cg', 'newton-cholesky', 'sag', 'saga'}, default='lbfgs'<br><br>Algorithm to use in the optimization problem. Default is 'lbfgs'.<br>To choose a solver, you might want to consider the following aspects:<br><br>- 'lbfgs' is a good default solver because it works reasonably well for a wide<br> class of problems.<br>- For :term:`multiclass` problems (`n_classes >= 3`), all solvers except<br> 'liblinear' minimize the full multinomial loss, 'liblinear' will raise an<br> error.<br>- 'newton-cholesky' is a good choice for<br> `n_samples` >> `n_features * n_classes`, especially with one-hot encoded<br> categorical features with rare categories. Be aware that the memory usage<br> of this solver has a quadratic dependency on `n_features * n_classes`<br> because it explicitly computes the full Hessian matrix.<br>- For small datasets, 'liblinear' is a good choice, whereas 'sag'<br> and 'saga' are faster for large ones;<br>- 'liblinear' can only handle binary classification by default. To apply a<br> one-versus-rest scheme for the multiclass setting one can wrap it with the<br> :class:`~sklearn.multiclass.OneVsRestClassifier`.<br><br>.. warning::<br> The choice of the algorithm depends on the penalty chosen (`l1_ratio=0`<br> for L2-penalty, `l1_ratio=1` for L1-penalty and `0 < l1_ratio < 1` for<br> Elastic-Net) and on (multinomial) multiclass support:<br><br> ================= ======================== ======================<br> solver l1_ratio multinomial multiclass<br> ================= ======================== ======================<br> 'lbfgs' l1_ratio=0 yes<br> 'liblinear' l1_ratio=1 or l1_ratio=0 no<br> 'newton-cg' l1_ratio=0 yes<br> 'newton-cholesky' l1_ratio=0 yes<br> 'sag' l1_ratio=0 yes<br> 'saga' 0<=l1_ratio<=1 yes<br> ================= ======================== ======================<br><br>.. note::<br> 'sag' and 'saga' fast convergence is only guaranteed on features<br> with approximately the same scale. You can preprocess the data with<br> a scaler from :mod:`sklearn.preprocessing`.<br><br>.. seealso::<br> Refer to the :ref:`User Guide <Logistic_regression>` for more<br> information regarding :class:`LogisticRegression` and more specifically the<br> :ref:`Table <logistic_regression_solvers>`<br> summarizing solver/penalty supports.<br><br>.. versionadded:: 0.17<br> Stochastic Average Gradient (SAG) descent solver. Multinomial support in<br> version 0.18.<br>.. versionadded:: 0.19<br> SAGA solver.<br>.. versionchanged:: 0.22<br> The default solver changed from 'liblinear' to 'lbfgs' in 0.22.<br>.. versionadded:: 1.2<br> newton-cholesky solver. Multinomial support in version 1.6. 'lbfgs'

<h1 id="%F0%9F%A4%96-Predictive-Churn-Model-%E2%80%93-Executive-Summary">🤖 Predictive Churn Model – Executive Summary¶</h1><h2 id="Business-Objective">Business Objective¶</h2><p>Build a machine learning model to predict whether a customer is likely to churn.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="Model-Used">Model Used¶</h2>
  • Logistic Regression
  • 80:20 Train-Test Split
<hr /> <h2 id="Key-Findings">Key Findings¶</h2>
  • The model predicts whether a customer is likely to churn based on customer demographics, subscription details, complaints, and satisfaction score.
  • Features with larger positive coefficients increase the likelihood of churn, while negative coefficients reduce it.
  • The model can help identify high-risk customers for proactive retention campaigns.
<hr /> <h2 id="Business-Recommendation">Business Recommendation¶</h2><p>Use the model to identify customers with a high probability of churn and offer targeted retention strategies such as discounts, personalized communication, or improved customer support.</p>
